extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and proof-assistant / formal-methods developers (mathematician community)
extracted.subtask_description: Deterministic compilation of proof traces from the Phase 11 Braid Theorem Prover into Lean 4 and Coq syntax, producing auditable ProofCertificates and demonstrating portability between provers via a common AST.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deterministic compilation
rubrics_metrics.description: The compiler deterministically compiles proof traces from the Phase 11 Braid Theorem Prover into target prover syntax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinism is verified across 26 tests (page notes: 'determinism verified across 26 tests'). The output should be byte-for-byte consistent across runs to support reproducibility and auditability.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1:1 syntactic compilation / structural isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: Braid -> Lean 1:1 syntactic compilation, exploiting structural isomorphism between Reidemeister moves R1/R2/R3 and Lean rewrite tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a direct, structure-preserving mapping from braid-prover constructs (notably Reidemeister moves) to the target prover's tactics/constructs so that the emitted code reflects the original proof structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-prover portability via common AST
rubrics_metrics.description: Coq portability bridge: same AST emits both Lean and Coq, demonstrating two-prover portability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the compiler around a shared abstract syntax tree (AST) that can be rendered into multiple proof-assistant syntaxes (Lean and Coq) to maximize portability.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProofCertificate auditability (fingerprint + metadata)
rubrics_metrics.description: ProofCertificate auditability: REI-LEAN-xxxxxxxx fingerprint + metadata; fingerprints are used to identify and audit proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emit a ProofCertificate including a deterministic fingerprint (e.g., REI-LEAN-xxxxxxxx) and accompanying metadata so third parties can verify provenance and integrity of compiled proofs; ensure fingerprint uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical verification via test-suite
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification of compiler properties (e.g., determinism) by running tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a test suite (the page cites 26 tests) to empirically verify key properties such as determinism and correctness of emitted proofs; document test coverage and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-to-end demonstrations on concrete samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide end-to-end demonstration on braid samples comparing generated Lean and Coq outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate the full pipeline on representative examples (the item reports 4 braid samples, total Lean 115 lines, Coq 130 lines) and report quantitative details (line counts, unique fingerprints) to show practical viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique fingerprinting for outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: All compiled outputs should have unique fingerprints to avoid collisions and aid auditability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that fingerprints produced for sample outputs are unique (the page states 'all fingerprints unique'); include procedures to detect and handle collisions.
